Extremely disappointed with the boarding care my dog received this past weekend. I dropped off my 20 lb pug on Friday with her dry food and a brand-new 13 oz can of wet food, along with clear feeding instructions: 1-2 tablespoon of wet food and 1 cup of kibble, twice daily.

When I picked her up Monday morning, I was shocked to find that the entire can of wet food had been used in just three days. At home, this same can typically lasts 7–10 days. When I asked about it, I was told that because she was not eating, the food was repeatedly discarded and replaced with new portions.

That same night after bringing her home, she developed severe diarrhea and soiled her pen, which is completely out of character for her. The problem continued into the following morning. A veterinary office should know better than to significantly change a dog’s feeding routine without contacting the owner, especially when it can lead to digestive issues.

This was an unacceptable experience, and I will not be returning. I hope management takes this seriously so it does not happen to other pets.

I don’t usually write reviews… but this place stays with you. From the moment you walk in, it’s too quiet. Not peaceful—just… still. Like the building is listening. The staff are warm, reassuring—but there are moments when their smiles fade just a little too quickly, like they almost forgot something important. My pet was called in before I even checked in. No one had said our name yet. When I asked about it, they just nodded and told me everything would be fine. In the exam room, I could’ve sworn I heard scratching behind the wall. Not loud—just enough to notice. The doctor didn’t react. None of them ever do. And the strangest part? My pet, who normally hates the vet, didn’t resist at all. Just stared past me… at something over my shoulder the whole time. We left with answers, good care, and everything we needed.
But I couldn’t shake the feeling that something else watched us leave. Still… I’d trust them with my pet again. Whatever they deal with here—they’re very, very good at it.

I love this vet! I took my leopard gecko, Mango, here when he got an abscess near his eye. I was so worried, but the antibiotic we got from the doctor healed him completely in a day or two. I came back with my basset hound, Pixie, to get her spayed. She's not a small dog, so needless to say I was pretty anxious about her having such a significant surgical procedure done, but it could not have gone more smoothly! Her wound healed amazingly, and she was back to running around in no time. Everyone here, from the receptionists to the techs to the doctors themselves, always greet you with a great attitude. Vets can be extremely expensive, so one thing I particularly like about this clinic is that they go to you with your bill and lay everything out for you with full transparency, willing to answer any questions, so that you have no doubts about where your money is going. The prices are also very reasonable. The last tech that attended me (wish I had gotten her name) was so upbeat and positive, Pixie adored her. The bottom line is that you can tell that this staff actually love the animals they take care of and that this is not simply just a job for them, and as an animal lover myself that's really important to me. I also want to give a special shout out to all the employees at the front desk. Whenever I call, they answer right away, and, unlike other vets, I don't feel like I'm bothering them. They don't put you on hold for ridiculous amounts of time and do their best to actually help you and get you seen as soon as you need!! The clinic itself is beautiful too, super nicely decorated and always clean and tidy. Overall, the service here is great, and they have gained a lifelong client out of me :)

Since my dog just ate few hr before coming to the clinic, I told them that I do want to go ahead with the procedure but that I’ll bring him back tomorrow, they did everything possible to tried to convince me to do it now even though they knew it isn’t safe to do this procedure with food in the stomach. Amarilis kept telling the front desk guy lies so he can convince me to the point that I was told that my dog was already shot and ready to go to surgery when it fact they had him inside the crate. I understand this is a business but where is the human side of it? Why do you care more about the $1300  than the dog safety? Seeing this makes me feel like for them it’s all about the money not the wellbeing of the pets. We are definitely not coming back to this place. Last year, I had paid for the clinic’s membership to take my dog regularly. In November 2024, my dog was unwell, so I took him in. They ran tests and said his kidneys were failing, and he had pancreatitis. They gave him IV fluids and treatment for the pancreatitis.

On the last day of treatment, they handed Baci back to me without any remarks. On the way home, I noticed he was bleeding from the mouth. When I checked more closely, he had a wound on his snout. I immediately returned to the clinic, but nobody knew what had happened to Baci. No one had seen anything, and they didn’t know how he had gotten that wound. This led me to believe that if they hadn’t caused it themselves, then my dog had been left without any kind of care or supervision.

I asked to speak with someone to explain what had happened, but no one attended me. They only gave me a spray to apply on the wound. The next day, they called me asking to bring Baci in for a check-up. As you can imagine, I never trusted them again. At one point, they even told me he might have bitten himself. Still, I went back to get answers, and that’s when a doctor finally saw us. Instead of clarifying what had happened, the conversation focused on the fact that Baci had very little time left, that there was NOTHING else to do for his kidneys, and that we should just give him Cerenia until he passed away…

And let me stress: they NEVER gave me an explanation about what had happened to Baci’s mouth. They never told us how he got that wound. Heartbroken, with Baci getting worse and without trusting them, we sought a second opinion at Doral Centre Animal Hospital. That’s when, first: THEY SAVED BACI. Second: they gave him TWO STITCHES on his snout (it was a deep wound).

While at Miami Springs they said Baci only had days left… at Doral Centre Animal Hospital they gave us hope. With daily fluids, Baci regained quality of life and went on living for almost another year — a year that, according to Miami Springs, he didn’t have.
